title: Machine learning methods for subpixel trajectory reconstruction in discretized position detectors
abstract: We evaluate machine-learning methods for sub-pixel position and trajectory-angle reconstruction in scintillator detectors. Geant4 simulations use two $50 \times 50$ cm plastic-scintillator planes separated by 30 cm, each represented by an $8 \times 8$ grid of 64 touching computational cells of pitch 6.25 cm. The plates are optically continuous. Photons reaching any outer face are absorbed and scored once in the pre-step cell. We sum the collected photon energies in each cell and normalize the signals to the plane total. Photodetectors and electronics are not simulated. We compare a transformer, a convolutional neural network (CNN), a multilayer perceptron (MLP), and an energy-weighted centroid. We compute directions from the two reconstructed positions. On a common 19,053-event test set, transformer and CNN median position errors (per-event means of the two planes' radial errors) are 0.18 and 0.23 cm, or 2.9% and 3.6% of the cell width. Their median space-angle errors are $0.35^\circ$ and $0.52^\circ$, compared with 1.03 cm and $1.90^\circ$ for the centroid and $4.21^\circ$ for an idealized Monte Carlo reference retaining only the traversed cell. The transformer has the lowest median errors, whereas the CNN has the lowest position- and angular-RMSE point estimates. Large-error tails limit the RMSE gains. Learned methods recover sub-pixel information in this idealized response. Establishing gains for muon tomography requires realistic optical coupling, photodetector response, and electronics.
